understanding.purpose: Show who owns each of three steps and the shared notes that apply to the whole sequence.
understanding.reading: Readers scan the steps and owners row by row, then read the merged Notes cell as context for all three steps. Wrapping in that cell can use the combined height of the three rows; heavier wrapping may make the table taller.
groups: Step and Owner form paired row-level identifiers; Notes applies to all three rows.
may_wrap: The shared Notes text can wrap naturally between words.

bad.why: The Step column is much wider than its short entries need, while the shared note is squeezed into nine lines. The resulting tall rows leave conspicuous empty space in the first two columns.

final.rationale: The preferred designs give the shared note most of the available width while keeping both short headers and all entries intact. The three step and owner pairs remain easy to scan, and the spanning note reads as a single block applying to all three rows. r0A and r1B have identical widths and renderings.

general: Allocate width according to content and reading relationships rather than making columns equal by default.
A cell spanning several rows can determine the height and whitespace of all those rows, so its wrapping needs to be judged against the whole table.
specific: Step and Owner contain short labels, leaving most of the width available for the long shared note.
The preferred widths keep the note to seven lines without splitting words.

final.tradeoffs: r0B gives the first two columns more breathing room, at the cost of an extra line in the note and taller rows. A designer might prefer that spacing even though the labels already fit comfortably in the preferred designs.
final.uncertain: The ranges are conservative estimates from the rendered candidates, not measured thresholds; intermediate widths may change individual line breaks. Treat them as coordinated alternatives within the 437px total, not independently selectable maxima.

A.why: Compact Step and Owner columns leave generous room for the shared note. The rows remain easy to scan, and the note wraps naturally.

B.why: The table scans cleanly, though slightly more width goes to the short labels and the note wraps a little less evenly than in A or E.

C.why: The labels are clear, but their wide columns leave the shared note noticeably narrower and make the rows taller.

D.why: The oversized Step column takes space from the long note, creating short lines and tall rows around very brief labels.

E.why: The compact label columns give the shared note ample width while keeping headers and row entries intact. The table has a clear, balanced rhythm.

F.why: The nearly equal columns force the long note into a narrow strip, producing many short lines and excessive empty space in the label columns.

reviews.unsure: A and E are very close; the rendered differences are too small to justify a confident preference between them.

A.why: All text fits and the three steps remain easy to scan, though Step and Owner take more width than their short entries need, leaving Notes somewhat narrow.

B.why: Compact Step and Owner columns give the shared note ample room, while the rows and headers remain clear and all words stay intact.

C.why: The narrow identifier columns leave generous space for the shared note, with clear row divisions and no broken words.

D.why: The wide Step column leaves unnecessary space beside short labels, while Notes wraps more often and makes the rows taller.

E.why: Step and Owner consume most of the width despite their short entries. The cramped Notes column produces a long, narrow block and excessive row height.

F.why: The short Step and Owner entries fit comfortably, and the wide Notes column keeps the shared paragraph readable with clear row divisions.

reviews.unsure: B, C and F are very close visually; their small differences in column widths and line breaks do not give any one a clear advantage.
